reason: The claim states that Au nanoparticle sizes decrease as the laser pulse energy rises, from the article's own TEM results (p.4, Table 3). Series 538584-s1 is exactly that experiment: four TEM geometric-diameter means at the four first-batch settings (96.6, 226, 286 and 318 mJ, stated on p.2 as 7.28, 17.03, 21.55 and 23.96 J/cm2), Au target in deionized water, 1064 nm, 8 ns, 1 Hz, 500 pulses. Same article, same medium class (water), same quantity (whole-particle TEM mean) and the same four runs; the article has no other series, so this is the only candidate and it is included by default.
caveats: Claim names pulse energy in mJ while the series x is fluence in J/cm2; the article states the correspondence for these same four settings on p.2, so the ordering is identical and no proxy beyond the article's own conversion is used. The highest-fluence point (23.96 J/cm2) is the histogram-derived mean of the Fig. 5(a) inset size distribution (11.28 nm), not the Table 3 scalar for the same sample (7.516 nm); both fall, so the shape is unaffected, but the pipeline's last point is not the value printed in the article's table. The fixed tolerances (0.10 or 0.20 x size) are independent of the SDs reported in the article (9.42, 11.74, 5.98 and 4.01 nm, without N). The claim covers only the four settings of a narrow 7.28-23.96 J/cm2 range. The article's second batch (repetition rate 2-8 Hz at fixed 96.6 mJ) is not part of this claim and yields no series: its four experiments are excluded as short_series with fewer than two points.
